minutes.headline: Committee approved FY18 line-item transfers and heard school nursing and technology FY19 budgets.
minutes.summary: The committee approved a set of fall line-item salary transfers prepared after a business office turnover, and authorized the chair to sign the FY17 year-end report. It gave initial approval to a student council convention trip and approved a calendar policy. It heard FY19 budget presentations from health services, technology and facilities, and honored a student golfer.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether MCAS scores should be sent home by backpack or mailed, given anxiety and young students opening them on the bus.

what_happened.line: The School Committee approved the fall line-item transfers, which reconcile personnel lines after summer reassignments and the business office changeover.
The transfers do not change the bottom line; they bring line items in step with actual spending before the next budget is built.
A Title I reduction moved one English language learner teacher to local funds and split another position between local and Title I money.
Motions to authorize the chair to sign the FY17 year-end report and to give initial approval to a student council convention trip were made; the results were not audible.
The committee heard FY19 presentations on health services, technology and facilities; the facilities proposal shows an overall reduction.

why_it_matters: Federal grant cuts such as Title I can shift staff salaries onto the local budget, which is mostly taxes, and overtime and substitute costs that are spent each year but not budgeted in lines show up as transfers rather than in the original budget.
Moving computer purchases from capital into the operating budget changes where technology costs appear in the FY19 school budget.
watch_next: Final approval of the student council convention trip, expected about four weeks before the trip.
A report on the Dean of Students position and its time split, which is to be reflected in the next budget.
